Theme

Household, washing & chores · Computing & programming

charger noun

for a phone or a battery

* our formation

* (our own formation) replētrum, replētrī n.

noun, second declension

Our formation, from replēre, our word for charging, with the suffix of instruments: arātrum, rāstrum, and from a verb in -ēre fulgētrum (Lewis & Short). It pairs with Traupman’s accumulātrum: the replētrum fills the accumulātrum. No reference work has a word for a charger.

Other words

  • * (our own formation) īnstrūmentum accumulātrō replendō

    phrase: the dative of purpose with a gerundive · also used · * our formation

    The same thing spelled out, for a first mention to someone who does not know the word.

Examples

  • Vīdistīne replētrum meum?

    Have you seen my charger?composed

See also charge, battery, plug.

SourcesLewis & Short: repleo · Lewis & Short: fulgetrum · Lewis & Short: instrumentum

No source has a Latin word for a charger; the word is built on our word for charging (see “charge”).

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
